LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES: ACTIVE AND PASSIVE VOICE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why should one use a variety of sentences? 2. How can one tell the doer and the receiver of an action in a sentence?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Sentences: Active and Passive Voice together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is boosted as the learner works with peers to create sentences thereby improving their

ability to express themselves in a variety of situations.

• Self-efficacy is enhanced as learners gain confidence by using passive and active voice in communication.

Values:
Respect is fostered as learners give their opinions during peer review of sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Career opportunities in sports is explored as learners read texts on the Olympics and underline active and passive sentences.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:
